bars.name: The Haberdasher
bars.desc: This rustic speakeasy is a hidden downtown gem, known for hosting lively whisky-fueled crawfish boils several times a year in its chic, secluded atmosphere.

bars.name: Fiori D’Italia
bars.desc: How did so many incredible bottles find their way to Alaska? Yet this unassuming Italian eatery, run by Yugoslavian owners, boasts an impressive array of rare whiskies from around the globe—a collection that remarkably survived a  devastating 2018 earthquake.

bars.name: Grey Hen Rx
bars.addr: 3626 E Indian School Rd., Phoenix, AZ
bars.desc: One of three “immersive” bars (presented by Barter & Shake Cocktail Entertainment) located within the Century Grand, this one is meant to resemble a Chinatown, Manhattan curiosity shop circa 1924. Along with Chinese food and exotic cocktails are a wealth of interesting whiskey pours spanning the globe.

bars.name: The Gladly
bars.desc: At this laid-back dining spot in the Biltmore neighborhood, over 350 world whiskies are on offer, including a slew of house single barrel picks, all available over à la minute ice balls crafted tableside.

bars.name: Cask 53 Whiskey Bar
bars.addr: 20751 N Pima Road Suite 105, Scottsdale, AZ
bars.desc: Seemingly a typical sports bar, until you eye the stellar backbar. Soon you’ll be scanning bottles more than the TVs playing Suns basketball and Cardinals football.

bars.name: Batch
bars.desc: This downtown bar claims the Grand Canyon State’s largest whisky list, with over 1,300 bottles soaring to the industrial ceilings of this small ‘shotgun’ space. It likewise offers one of the more unusual bar-bite pairings on this list: glazed and frosted craft doughnuts made in-house—some that are boozy themselves!

bars.name: Vault
bars.addr: 112 W Center St, Suite B001, Fayetteville, AR
bars.desc:
Set in a former bank vault, this bar’s concrete and steel design with black oak tables and charred white oak walls 
is meant to aesthetically conjure distillation and barrel-aging. One can’t help but admire the patina of the bar as you sip through Arkansas’s most impressive bourbon list.

bars.name: Acme Bar & Company
bars.desc: This Berkeley institution has been a neighborhood favorite for over two decades, offering expertly curated whisky flights to its loyal regulars.

bars.name: CIR Lounge
bars.addr: 18120 Brookhurst St., Suite 2, Fountain Valley, CA
bars.desc: This elegant Orange County cocktail spot balances Japanese and Mediterranean flavors, with drinks named after simple, freshly-sourced ingredients (i.e. Green Tea, made with Japanese whisky, St-Germain, green tea, and honey) and a formidable list of Japanese whiskies.

bars.name: Johnny’s Neighborhood Saloon
bars.desc: This longtime O.C. stalwart, set in a strip mall, is a raucous dive bar with Americana plastered on the walls, artisan pizza, and a better whisky selection than you’d ever expect.

bars.name: The Pines Modern Steakhouse
bars.addr: 777 San Manuel Blvd S, Highland, CA 92346
bars.desc: The Pines Modern Steakhouse showcases Collection 86, an extraordinary selection of rare and vintage wines and spirits, including one of the world’s most impressive whiskey collections.

bars.name: Seven Grand / Bar Jackalope
bars.addr: 515 W 7th St., 2nd floor, Los Angeles, CA
bars.desc: With additional locations in San Diego, Denver, and Austin, the original DTLA Seven Grand still stands out— especially with its tucked-away, 18-seat Bar Jackalope offering an intimate Japanese whisky experience.

bars.name: Wolf & Crane
bars.desc: This cozy Little Tokyo bar boldly boasts that they have the largest Japanese whisky collection in the U.S., making it a must-visit for whisky lovers in downtown LA.

bars.name: Old Lightning
bars.addr: 2905 W Washington Blvd, Marina Del Rey, CA
bars.desc: If the pandemic nearly put this rare-spirits speakeasy out of business, it has returned better than ever with a collection of modern rarities and vintage masterpieces from the past. Old Lightning remains one of the best places in the country to drink something special.

bars.name: The Roost
bars.desc: This quaint bar (and former fried chicken joint) crams over 700 rare and unique bottles everywhere from floor to ceiling.

bars.name: Aero Club Bar
bars.desc: A one-time pilot’s bar, the divey Aero Club still entertains with pool tables, a jukebox, and an impressive wall featuring over 800 whiskies.

bars.name: Raised by Wolves
bars.addr: 4301 La Jolla Village Drive, #2030, San Diego, CA
bars.desc: With a round bar that is surely one of the most beautiful in the world, “Wolves” likewise dazzles with an array of private barrel selections and vintage spirits.

bars.name: The Whiskey House
bars.desc: This Gaslamp Quarter bar holds a Guinness Record for largest whisky selection—currently 93 pages long!—with rare bottlings from unexpected places like Israel, Switzerland, and the Czech Republic.

bars.name: Bottle Club Pub
bars.addr: 555 Geary St. at Shannon St, San Francisco, CA
bars.desc: Dedicated to those garish bourbon decanters from the 50s, 60s, and 70s, this quirky San Francisco bar offers a taste of bourbon’s “glut” era.

bars.name: Elixir
bars.desc: San Francisco’s second-oldest saloon (since 1858!) now has more elevated pours than they might have had in the post-Gold Rush era.

bars.name: Rickhouse
bars.desc: A staple of Financial District drinkers, its interior design incorporates old whiskey barrels, staves, and charred brick from before 1906’s earthquake.

bars.name: Hops & Scotch
bars.addr: 7001 Sunne Lane Suite #100, Walnut Creek, CA
bars.desc: The East Bay’s top spot for whisky offers plenty of single barrel picks in a massive leather-bound “bible” counting nearly 200 pages.

bars.name: The Bluegrass Coffee & Bourbon Lounge
bars.desc: With two locations in this historic town northwest of Denver, The Bluegrass might be the earliest-opening whisky bar in America (7 a.m.) and almost certainly the only one that also roasts its own coffee beans.

bars.name: J-Bar at Hotel Jerome
bars.desc: Once a haven for gold miners and Hunter S. Thompson, this historic Aspen bar remains the town’s top spot for a stellar whisky selection.

bars.name: Whiskey Bar at Cascades Restaurant
bars.addr: 333 E Wonderview Ave, Estes Park, CO
bars.desc: Set inside The Shining-inspired Stanley Hotel, you can get a Redrum Punch (natch) or choose from the state’s largest selection of single malt scotch. All work and no play makes Jack a thirsty boy.

bars.name: The Whisk(e)y
bars.addr: 214 S College Ave. #2, Fort Collins, CO
bars.desc: In a craft beer town, this Fort Collins bar stands out with a staggering 2,250 whisky options, including its house blend, “Pappy Juice.”

bars.name: Owl Shop
bars.desc: Just blocks from Yale’s campus, this plush lounge is one of the finest tobacconists in the country, even blending its own pipe tobacco. It’s also a full cocktail bar offering over 200 whiskies to pair with any number of great cigars.

bars.name: Barrel
bars.addr: 613 Pennsylvania Ave. SE 2nd floor, Washington, DC
bars.desc: Now over a decade old, this Capitol Hill joint can go toe-to-toe with any whisky collection in the city. A popular brunch spot, on weekends you’ll see young staffers fighting off hangovers with Southern grub (think chicken & waffles) and straight bourbon.

bars.name: Jack Rose Dining Saloon
bars.desc: Bill Thomas’s whisky emporium is the granddaddy of American whisky bars…and still one of the best, with arguably the most varied and interesting whisky list in the country. A mecca for any serious whisky connoisseur.

bars.name: The Fountain Inn
bars.desc: This Georgetown bar is in a building from 1783 that was once the most important bar in American history (Suter’s Tavern, where Washington once slept and Jefferson and Adams once debated). These days the madeira of the 1700s has been swapped for trendy allocated pours, house single barrels, and even vintage bottles.

bars.name: Warren
bars.desc: With an interior chock full of velvet and leather, this restaurant evokes a sort of Rat Pack-era dinner club. It also offers several cuts of A5 wagyu steak and one of Florida’s biggest whisky collections.

bars.name: Whiskey Neat
bars.desc: Boasting a motto of “rare whiskeys you can’t find elsewhere,” that might actually be true in this spot a few blocks from the beach. For cocktail fans, the bar offers five different house Old Fashioneds.

bars.name: Old Hickory Whiskey Bar
bars.desc: Set in the state’s panhandle, this bar boasts an unmatched selection of brown spirits.

bars.name: Julep Palm Valley
bars.addr: 154 Canal Blvd, Ponte Vedra Beach, FL
bars.desc: Set in the land of golf courses—the famed TPC Sawgrass is nearby—you’ll see plenty of duffers using this spot as the 19th hole.

bars.name: Local Three Kitchen & Bar
bars.desc: This chef-driven urban restaurant offers adventurous Southern fare alongside an ample bourbon selection.

bars.name: Bar Leather Apron
bars.addr: 745 Fort Street Mall Suite #127, Honolulu, HI
bars.desc: In downtown Honolulu, this bar combines Japanese whisky with island-inspired cocktails like a Matcha Old Fashioned, bringing drinkers a true taste of Hawaii.

bars.name: Whiskey Bar
bars.desc: With 200 whiskies lining the reclaimed wood walls, this Boise bar offers a rustic setting for sipping and savoring.

bars.name: Big Star
bars.desc: Set in a converted 1940s gas station, Big Star (now with several locations around Chicagoland) is known for rowdy taco feasts paired with house-picked pours.

bars.name: Delilah’s
bars.desc: Delilah’s remains a Chicago staple, with a rowdy reputation for loud music and strong whisky. You’ll be stunned by the rarities housed in such a divey atmosphere.

bars.name: Longman & Eagle
bars.desc: Surely the best place to drink whisky and then go to sleep, this urban inn features six guest rooms upstairs.

bars.name: Mordecai
bars.desc: Right across the street from Wrigley Field, located in the Hotel Zachary—and named after legendary Cubs hurler “Three Finger” Brown—this handsomely designed spot is better on non-game days, when one can quietly contemplate the outstanding rarities and vintage pours available.

bars.name: Slightly Toasted
bars.desc: Claiming Chitown’s largest whisky collection, this impressive West Loop spot has over 900 unique options including more than 30 private barrel picks and a vintage list totaling into the two-hundreds.

bars.name: The Office
bars.desc: Beneath Michelin-starred Alinea’s cocktail bar, this tucked-away lounge offers high-end classics and rare vintage spirits alongside the expected avant-garde bites.

bars.name: Untitled Supper Club
bars.desc: This massive 18,000 square-foot restaurant has an equally prodigious whisky menu. The Prohibition-era aesthetic is perfect for the weekly musical and cabaret performances.

bars.name: Hardware
bars.addr: 2000 W Orchard Rd, North Aurora, IL
bars.desc: This so-called “sustainable gastropub” (and brewery) in the Chicago suburbs has one of the most gorgeous restaurant designs you’ll ever see, with reclaimed architecture and living walls. It also claims over 1,000 unique whiskies including local allotted private barrels and house blends.

bars.name: St. Elmo Steak House
bars.desc: Downtown Indianapolis’s iconic chophouse serves the famed Elmo Cola—a whisky-infused concoction topped with “drunken” cherries.

bars.name: Alleged Lee’s
bars.addr: 510 E Grand Ave, Des Moines, IA
bars.desc: This offbeat spot in the East Village has bi-monthly drag bingo, seasonal cocktails, and the city’s best whisky selection.

bars.name: The Monarch
bars.desc: This art-filled whisky haven set in the Delano district rewards regulars with prizes for trying 25 different whiskies.

bars.name: The Kitchen & Bar
bars.desc: Located inside Bardstown Bourbon Company’s wonderland of a facility, this daytime spot offers craft cocktails, rare whiskies, and one of the most impressive vintage spirits libraries around, with bottles dating back to the 19th century.

bars.name: Revival
bars.desc: These two-in-one vintage bottle shops and full-service bars offer a century’s worth of bourbon history with vintage pours and vintage cocktails.

bars.name: Smoke Justis
bars.desc: What could go better with bourbon than smoked meats and sports on the myriad TVs in this whiskey bar in Covington’s historic Citizens Telephone Building?

bars.name: Wiseguy Lounge
bars.desc: These are a series of low-lit bourbon and cocktail-fueled speakeasies hidden among more than a dozen Goodfellas Pizzerias in four states (Kentucky, Ohio, Tennessee, and Indiana).

bars.name: Justins’ House of Bourbon
bars.desc: Owned and run by longtime vintage spirits collectors, both locations showcase a stunning selection of rare and vintage bottles available for tasting and sale.

bars.name: Bluegrass Tavern
bars.desc: By now an O.G. among the state’s whisky bars, great bottles are jammed into every single nook and cranny of this relaxed tavern.

bars.name: Bourbon on Rye
bars.desc: Bourbon flights and vintage chandeliers create the perfect atmosphere at this moody, elegant whisky haven.

bars.name: bar Vetti
bars.desc: This regional Italian spot is right off of downtown’s Whiskey Row, making it a popular dinner spot amongst distillery employees and others in the industry. In turn, it offers a stellar bourbon and cocktail list, not to mention great Italian wine and amaro.

bars.name: Doc Crow’s Southern Smokehouse and Raw Bar
bars.desc: Located on the city’s Whiskey Row, in a former distillery warehouse built in 1869, this expansive spot offers barbecue, Southern favorites, and, oh yeah, more than 2,000 whiskies.

bars.name: Neat Bourbon Bar + Bottle Shop
bars.desc: Set in the hip NuLu neighborhood, this plush lounge offers dusty whiskies (for pours and as bottles to go) from legendary and now-defunct distilleries, all at fair prices that will make you think you might have time-traveled yourself. In 2025, they opened a second location in Bardstown.

bars.name: North of Bourbon
bars.desc: Guests dine inside oversized bourbon barrels at this Creole/Cajun restaurant—peppered catfish nuggets and gumbo z’herbes—while sipping fancified bourbon cocktails (the Frozen Kentucky Coffee, inspired by New Orleans’s Erin Rose, is not to miss).

bars.name: Proof on Main
bars.desc: This stylish bar in the 21c Museum Hotel showcases dozens of exclusive barrel picks from Kentucky’s best-known distilleries.

bars.name: SEVEN Cocktails + Bourbon
bars.desc: This new spot in NuLu might be the most elevated drinking spot in town. There are “premium” cocktails, like an A5 Wagyu fat-washed Old-Fashioned, as well as vintage spirits galore.

bars.name: The Last Refuge
bars.desc: This self-proclaimed “High Church of Bourbon” (built in a deconsecrated church) is partly owned by Bob Dylan and offers bottles all the way to the top of its vaulted ceiling.

bars.name: The Pearl of Germantown
bars.desc: The neighborhood dive has an elite single barrel program and relaxed vibes that go all night.

bars.name: Tartan House
bars.desc: This moody bar in a converted house in Butchertown offers some of the city’s most sophisticated cocktails alongside a carefully curated selection of great whiskies.

bars.name: Barrel & Bond
bars.desc: Housed in a 150 year old building in downtown, you could call this restaurant whisky-driven, as bites are paired with whisky, not the reverse.

bars.name: Freight House
bars.desc: Nestled in another 150 year old building, this spot pairs whisky with hearty bites, creating a truly whisky-centric dining experience.

bars.name: Watch Hill Proper
bars.desc: No longer just a members-only bar, this suburban Louisville spot has one of the most impressive bourbon walls in the country.

bars.name: CURE
bars.desc: CURE revitalized New Orleans’s cocktail scene over a decade ago with their expertly crafted drinks, including an “Extra Fancy Sazerac” built on super-premium, high-proof ryes.

bars.name: Dickie Brennan’s Bourbon House
bars.desc: As the headquarters of the New Orleans Bourbon Society, this lively seafood and oyster bar on Bourbon Street regularly hosts events and tastings featuring some of the industry’s biggest names.

bars.name: The Independent Ice Co.
bars.desc: Inspired by long-gone Kennebec River ice harvesters—yes, that was once how you got your ice—you can also opt for neat pours alongside the expected lobster rolls.

bars.name: Barfly’s
bars.desc: A neighborhood pub that punches above its weight when it comes to the brown stuff, with some 650 bourbons and scotches, not to mention a slew of fun, personal pan pizzas (like one meant to resemble a Big Mac).

bars.name: DRY 85
bars.desc: Set right in downtown, this industrial-style speakeasy is the perfect place to sneak a dram.

bars.name: Citizen Public House & Oyster Bar
bars.desc: About a block away from home plate, this Fenway tavern is famous for its family-style pig roasts, slow-cooked for 14 hours, along with a curated list of over 400 whiskies.

bars.name: Gigantic Bar
bars.desc: This cocktail bar also offers vintage whisky in every category, with Maryland ryes from the 1940s and White Horse from back when Lagavulin was a mere blending component.

bars.name: The Last Word
bars.addr: 301 W Huron St, Ann Arbor, MI
bars.desc: Though named after the gin-and-Chartreuse classic, this hip joint also has a “whiskey fascination,” offering hundreds of bottles in an economical one-ounce tasting size—perfect for the grad students that often wander in.

bars.name: The Sugar House
bars.desc: Long regarded as the best cocktail bar in Motor City, this Corktown favorite is equally celebrated for its deep whisky list, with plenty of house single barrels to explore.

bars.name: Butter Run Saloon
bars.addr: 27626 Harper Ave., St. Clair Shores, MI
bars.desc: This unassuming Detroit-area bar, humorously named after those grocery store “errands,” offers hearty meals and an impressive whisky selection to match.

bars.name: Gori Gori Peku
bars.addr: 33 North First Ave., 2nd Floor, Minneapolis, MN
bars.desc: Across the hall from Japanese-born chef Shigeyuki Furukawa’s James Beard-nominated omakase and kaiseki tasting menu counter, this darkly-lit spot is similarly refined and contemplative, with Japanese whiskies and transportative cocktails.

bars.name: Volstead House
bars.addr: 1278 Lone Oak Rd., St. Paul, MN
bars.desc: Named after the act that kicked off the “noble experiment” of Prohibition, this Twin Cities bar offers cocktails from the pre-Pro era, like the Blood and Sand, an unusual scotch and orange juice drink named after a Rudolph Valentino silent film from 1922.

bars.name: MatchStick Restaurant and Spirits
bars.desc: This farm-to-table restaurant located in the Hotel Crosby impresses with over 700 spirits, specializing in whisky from every corner of the globe.

bars.name: The Manship
bars.desc: Wood-fired is the name of the game at this Mediterranean-inspired restaurant that also happens to have the largest whisky list in the state.

bars.name: The Rack House Kitchen Wine Whiskey
bars.desc: This Missouri restaurant’s whisky club rewards guests for exploring their extensive selection—every 25 whiskies earns you fun prizes like premium flights or a Barrel Aged Manhattan.

bars.name: Copper Whiskey Bar & Grill
bars.desc: This bar offers whisky enthusiasts the chance to transform any pour into a classic cocktail like an Old Fashioned or Sazerac for just a few extra bucks.

bars.name: Single Barrel
bars.desc: As the name suggests, this chophouse offers hundreds of limited-edition bourbons and ryes to accompany their hearty fare.

bars.name: Stage Left Steak
bars.desc: Arguably the first modern cocktail bar in America, opening in 1992, well before the recent cocktail renaissance. Today, this greenmarket-driven steak house also has a world class wine cellar and a top-notch whisky program.

bars.name: Radish & Rye
bars.desc: This classy “farm-inspired” restaurant offers Southern and New Orleans-style cuisine (fried green tomatoes, gulf shrimp, chicken & waffles) alongside a celebration of American bourbons and ryes.

bars.name: Sanford’s Restaurant
bars.desc: Queens’s top whisky bar has an extensive collection one can enjoy in a relaxed pub-like environment.

bars.name: Fool Proof
bars.desc: Only in Brooklyn would a whisky bar offer beet burrata and vegan tartare. Alas, they do indeed pair well with the elevated cocktails and lengthy international whisky list.

bars.name: The Moonlight Mile
bars.desc: Co-owner Garry Embry (along with his wife Becky) was born and raised in Louisville. And yet there’s a surprising amount of great whiskey here from the other 49 states, as well as plenty of offbeat whisky cocktails.

bars.name: The Richardson
bars.desc: Set on the border between Williamsburg and Greenpoint, the bartenders may wear ties but this spot is anything but stuffy. House cocktails like the  Kentucky Tesseract and The Perfect Crime are made with the bar’s own private barrel picks.

bars.name: Travel Bar
bars.desc: This family-friendly neighborhood bar in South Brooklyn draws whisky fans from across the city, thanks to its curated collection of rare pours.

bars.name: Lucky Day Whiskey Bar
bars.desc: Western New York’s best whisky bar has 800 options, including many of the uber-allocated variety. The food is equally expense account-level with dry-aged rib eyes and seafood towers.

bars.name: Bar Moga
bars.addr: 128 W. Houston St., New York, NY
bars.desc: This 1920s-era Japanese-inspired cocktail bar offers jazz music, shoku (Japanese comfort food, like katsu sandos) and Japanese-made booze including shochu, umeshu, and tons of single malts.

bars.name: Brandy Library
bars.addr: 25 N Moore St., New York, NY
bars.desc: This Tribeca institution  has been a refined destination for whisky aficionados looking for an evening of luxury since 2004.

bars.name: Copper & Oak
bars.desc: This Lower East Side shoebox makes the most of its small space, boasting an impressive selection of rare drams.

bars.name: Shinjis Bar
bars.desc: This 18-seat half-arc bar has stellar cocktails, experimental shots, one of the largest Japanese whisky selections in the city, and tableside handroll service.

bars.name: Sip & Guzzle
bars.desc: Famed barmen Shingo Gokan’s and Steve Schneider’s downtown den offers classic cocktails at street level and more experimental Japanese-style drinks in the basement. The izakaya and Japanese street food (from former Alinea executive chef Mike Bagale) is not to be missed.

bars.name: The Dead Rabbit
bars.desc: This modernized and elevated Irish pub also lays claim to one of the most extensive Irish whiskey collections in the U.S.

bars.name: The Flatiron Room
bars.desc: Its two large midtown spaces offer roomy banquettes, gorgeous decor, and striking stages where musicians perform every night. An elevated dinner menu and plenty of smokin’ cocktails will delight any whisky fan.

bars.name: Whisky Room at Nakaji
bars.desc: Tucked inside this pricy, edomae-style sushi counter, the bar offers seasonal cocktails and rare Japanese whiskies, as well as Michelin-caliber otsumami plates and a daily selection of premium sea urchins.

bars.name: Al’s Wine & Whiskey Lounge
bars.desc: With a whisky selection so large it requires a library ladder, this Syracuse spot is a must-visit for anyone looking to explore rare bottles.

bars.name: Archie’s Tap and Table
bars.desc: This snug spot, right near the water on City Island, offers fine dining-level cuisine and a shockingly robust whisky list, with allocated bottles galore.

bars.name: Traghaven Whiskey Pub
bars.desc: For nearly a decade this Hudson Valley pub has quietly offered the largest selection of Irish whiskey in the States.

bars.name: Herbs & Rye
bars.addr: 3713 W Sahara Ave., Las Vegas, NV
bars.desc: Located off the Strip in a simple strip mall, this stylish bar evokes the glamor of Vegas’s past, serving classic cocktails and an impressive range of whiskies.

bars.name: Death & Taxes
bars.desc: This upscale bar and bottle shop features some of the best nightly tasting events in Sin City.

bars.name: The Crunkleton
bars.addr: 320 West Franklin St., Chapel Hill, NC
bars.desc: Whisky expert Gary Crunkleton’s eponymous bars offer one of the most impressive whisky collections in the South, alongside vintage cocktails.

bars.name: The Noble Hare
bars.desc: This speakeasy-style lounge with velvet banquettes and a granite bar top is designed for contemplative sipping and conversation, the former spurring on the latter thanks to a collection of over 100 whiskies.

bars.name: The Alibi Bourbon and Cocktail Lounge
bars.desc: Located in downtown’s Short North district, this bar offers a rich selection of beer, bourbon, and Prohibition-era cocktails.

bars.name: Speak of the Devil
bars.desc: This hidden downtown gem offers a whisky selection that rivals the best of Cleveland’s bars, housed in a laid-back neighborhood setting.

bars.name: The Winston
bars.desc: With two locations in greater Oklahoma City, this family-friendly restaurant offers elevated pub fare with a Southern twist, like chicken-fried filet mignon, but they really shine with their whisky list. The back wall has bar-to-ceiling options like private picks and allocated bottlings. Happy hour cocktails are as cheap as $3.95 starting at 3 p.m and going up a buck an hour.

bars.name: The Daley
bars.desc: Located in the capital city's trendy Paseo Arts District, the den-like like bars—filled with interesting books and trinkets—offers a whiskey "library" and TK. As the bar component of James Beard-nominated restaurant FRIDA Southwest, the food is great too with elevated bar bites like pigs in a blanket and Reubens.

bars.name: Valkyrie
bars.desc: Set in downtown Tulsa's Arts District, this laid-back bar offers a motto of “playfully serving serious drinks.” Besides offbeat takes on classics—the Shukette is a white Manhattan made with tahini fat-washed bourbon— the back bar offers a formidable wall of whiskey from all the major regions.

bars.name: Blaylock’s
bars.desc: The food menu is focused almost exclusively on boards—as in cheese, charcuterie, paté, and more—but the whisky, of course, comes in a glass.

bars.name: Multnomah Whisk(e)y Library
bars.desc: One of the country’s most famous whisky destinations offers paid memberships, granting priority access to its massive collection of rare bottles, exclusive events, and single-barrel selections.

bars.name: Paddy’s Bar and Grill
bars.desc: Located in the historic Ira F. Powers building, the bar is Irish to the teeth, with house-made shepherd’s pie, perfect pints of Guinness, the Guinness Record for the largest Irish Coffee ever made...and the most Irish whiskey in the City of Roses.

bars.name: Paydirt
bars.desc: “Paydirt has too much whiskey” reads the website landing page for this drinking establishment set in an 8,000

bars.name: Scotch Lodge
bars.desc: Forget the name; bourbon lovers and cocktail enthusiasts will also will find plenty of top-shelf selections at this ode to whisky.

bars.name: The Warren
bars.desc: This downtown bar offers Highballs on tap from a Highball machine alongside  made-to-order sushi.

bars.name: Ashton Cigar Bar
bars.desc: One of the country’s best cigar bars is also a stellar spot for whisky in the heart of the Cradle of Liberty.

bars.name: Alquimia Whisky Bar & Tapas
bars.desc: The house sangria and coquito are both unexpectedly made with whisky at this island spot that offers empanadas and chorizo cooked in rye to munch on.

bars.name: The East End
bars.desc: Run by former “MasterChef” contestant Hannah Weaver, this culinary-focused tavern offers an ample whisky list.

bars.name: Paddock & Whisky
bars.desc: The bar’s original location on James Island is a petite salute to fine bourbon, while a larger sister restaurant in North Charleston is set in a former bank building with whiskies stocked all the way to the top of its high ceilings.

bars.name: Bourbon
bars.desc: This bar pairs Louisiana-inspired cuisine with South Carolina’s largest whisky list.

bars.name: Neat Bourbon Bar
bars.desc: The low-slung ceilings give a warm feel to this Main Street Greenville spot with an array of interesting pours. The two others locations are also stellar.

bars.name: The Barrel House
bars.desc: There’s a waffle bar available every Sunday morning for brunch, while the evenings skew more toward private barrel picks and the best allocated whisky list in the Dakotas.

bars.name: The Fox Bar & Cocktail Club
bars.desc: Tucked away east of downtown, this speakeasy offers low-lit private booths, vegan-friendly bar bites, and a stellar whisky selection for adventurous palates.

bars.name: Belle Tavern
bars.desc: Tucked in an obscure alley downtown, this whisky bar boasts the largest selection in the city, with flights and creative house cocktails like the Three Whiskey Old Fashioned.

bars.name: Barrel Proof
bars.desc: This Germantown neighborhood joint (with a second location in NOLA’s Garden District) claims they don’t even know how many whiskies they have—they quit counting a long time ago.

bars.name: Gertie’s Bar at The 404 Kitchen
bars.desc: Located in The Gulch neighborhood, downstairs from The 404 Kitchen, this Music City favorite offers an extensive whisky list and a modern European menu.

bars.name: Nickel City
bars.desc: The most fun whisky bar in the Lone Star State is now in Houston and Fort Worth too;  chili dogs, sliders, and frozen Irish coffee is the move, though there are plenty of elite whisky pours as well.

bars.name: The Standard Pour
bars.desc: This laid-back neighborhood cocktail lounge delivers elevated mixology and tasty bar bites.

bars.name: Anvil Bar & Refuge
bars.addr: 1424 Westheimer Rd. Suite B, Houston, TX
bars.desc: This legendary Houston spot offers a “Captain’s List” featuring nearly 30 pages of whisky, plus a rotating top-100 cocktail list for those seeking even more variety.

bars.name: Permission Whiskey & Service Co.
bars.desc: At this high-end cocktail bar in the Woodland Heights neighborhood, regulars can rent private lockers to store special spirits and flex when entertaining friends.

bars.name: Poison Girl
bars.addr: 1641 Westheimer Rd. Suite B, Houston, TX
bars.desc: In the city’s eclectic Montrose neighborhood, this pinup-inspired dive boasts a rich American whiskey collection alongside vintage pinball machines.

bars.name: Reserve 101
bars.desc: This downtown spot has gone all-in on the dusty booze business with a growing selection of vintage bottles, the most rare of which soar into the four-figures-an-ounce territory.

bars.name: Bar 1919
bars.addr: 1420 S. Alamo St., San Antonio, TX
bars.desc: Inspired by the pre-Prohibition era—the name tells you the year that would be—this dimly-lit basement space harkens back to the great whiskies and whisky cocktails of the time.

bars.name: J.S. Barnett’s Whiskey House
bars.desc: Claiming the largest collection of whisky in the state with over 1,200 bottles from the U.S., Scotland, Japan, and, of course, the Republic of Texas.

bars.name: Whiskey Street
bars.addr: 323 South Main Street, Salt Lake City, UT
bars.desc: In August of 2025, a fire ravaged downtown SLC’s Main Street and, in turn, Whiskey Street sustained substantial damage. The owners remain committed to rising from the ashes and reopening their salute to whisky and boozy food.

bars.name: Prohibition Pig
bars.desc: In a state with some of the best breweries in the nation, this smoked-meats joint has a brewery just around the corner, but offers a sublime spirits list here, with plenty of great whisky when an IPA just won’t cut it.

bars.name: Virtue Feed & Grain
bars.desc: This beautiful two-story restaurant was once a feed and grain warehouse in the 1800s. Today it offers some of the best bottles in the state, handpicked by Kentucky Colonel Tom “Big T” Gale.

bars.name: MacMillian Whisky Room
bars.desc: This raucous restaurant in the Mosaic District just might have northern Virginia’s largest whisky selection.

bars.name: Rebellion
bars.desc: Opened by two military veterans who proudly offer local barrel picks from places like Catoctin Creek and A. Smith Bowman.

bars.name: Vault & Cellar
bars.desc: Chef Kari Rushing brings the flavors of Appalachia (fried catfish, wild boar sausage)  to this homey spot, and that includes bourbon, of which she has personally curated over 300 bottles.

bars.name: McCormack’s Big Whisky Grill
bars.addr: 1420 N Parham Rd. k210, Richmond, VA
bars.desc: This strip mall restaurant in the ’burbs offers an epic wall of whisky.

bars.name: Whisky by John Howie
bars.desc: An offshoot of the chef’s eponymous next-door steakhouse, this PNW-inspired lounge offers an open kitchen and hundreds of global whiskies.

bars.name: Ballard Cut
bars.desc: In the Ballard neighborhood, this spots pair seasonal, local dish with rare whisky, specifically the Japanese single malt variety.

bars.name: Canon Whiskey and Bitters Emporium
bars.desc: Jamie Boudreau’s paean to whisky manages to cram rare and vintage bottles into every spare inch of this snug Capitol Hill space; it’s long been one of the most acclaimed cocktail bars in the country, with vintage mixed drinks to boot.

bars.name: Radiator Whiskey
bars.desc: This meat-mad restaurant offers whiskies “on tap” from The Big Barrel, an Instagram-worthy giant barrelhead in the middle of the backbar.

bars.name: The Doctor’s Office
bars.desc: Dr. Matthew Powell, a hospital medicine specialist and a longtime cocktail geek, designed this 12-seat tasting room to recall the alleyway bars of Tokyo’s Shinjuku Golden Gai district. The bar offers a healthy list of rare single malts, some dusty Suntory from the 1970s, vintage bourbon once owned by Howard Hughes, and the best damn flaming Spanish coffee on Earth.

bars.name: Cask & Ale
bars.desc: This amiable tavern near the university offers whisky from all categories, though the Old Fashioneds will, of course, be made with brandy, per local tradition.

bars.name: Local
bars.desc: Apres-ski with whisky at this resort-town hot spot and modern steakhouse, with an in-house butchery providing classic and specialty cuts of locally ranched meats and game to match a well-rounded whisky list of nearly 100 bottles, more than a few Wyoming-made.
